```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Brazil drought measures pilot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This R Markdown file starts from the monthly ERA5-Land ADM2 drought file and
# walks through the main choices for the drought part of the rainfall-mortality
# project.
#
# The Brazil pilot looks at raw rainfall, 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month rainfall
# totals, the prior-20-year baseline, 5th/10th percentile thresholds, z-scores,
# rainfall deficits, monthly-to-annual summaries, and selected Brazil drought
# episodes.
#
# The point is to understand what each measure is capturing before deciding
# which annual drought variables should move into the mortality panel.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------
# Packages and paths
# -----------------------------

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(kableExtra)
library(plotly)
library(scales)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(htmltools)
library(magrittr)

# Turn off spherical geometry so Brazil shapefile operations stay predictable
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Monthly drought file from 01 and Brazil ADM2 boundaries for maps
drought_root <- "/project/cil/gcp/estimation/rainfall-mortality/climate_data/ERA5-LAND/drought"
monthly_file <- file.path(drought_root, "monthly", "era5land_admin_drought_monthly_bra.rds")
bra_shape_file <- "/project/cil/norgay/Global_ACP/MORTALITY/Replication_2018/2_Data/Raw/Countries/BRA/Shapefile/BRA_adm2.shp"

stopifnot(file.exists(monthly_file))

# Windows and display periods used throughout the diagnostic
windows <- c(1, 3, 6, 12)
period_levels <- c("1980-1990", "1991-2010", "2011-2024")

# -----------------------------
# Read monthly drought measures
# -----------------------------

# Population-weighted monthly measures used in this diagnostic
monthly_columns <- c(
  "climate_country", "region_id", "unsupported_baseline_region",
  "date_month", "year", "month_number",
  sprintf("rain_mm_%02dm_pop", windows),
  sprintf("percentile_%02dm_pop", windows),
  sprintf("z_%02dm_pop", windows),
  sprintf("deficit_mm_%02dm_pop", windows),
  "rs_drought_12m_pop",
  "rs_logdev_12m_pop",
  "rs_pctdev_12m_pop"
)

monthly <- readRDS(monthly_file)
setDT(monthly)

# Main diagnostics use population-weighted measures for supported Brazil ADM2s
monthly <- monthly[, intersect(monthly_columns, names(monthly)), with = FALSE]
monthly <- monthly[
  climate_country == "BRA" &
    unsupported_baseline_region == FALSE]

monthly[, date_month := as.IDate(date_month)]

# Continuous month index
monthly[, month_index := year * 12 + month_number]

# Period labels are only for display tables
monthly[
  ,
  Period := fcase(
    year <= 1990, "1980-1990",
    year <= 2010, "1991-2010",
    default = "2011-2024"
  )
]
monthly[, Period := factor(Period, levels = period_levels)]

# -----------------------------
# Selected ADM2s
# -----------------------------

# Four ADM2s with different rainfall levels, seasons, and known low-rainfall periods
selected_places <- data.table(
  region_id = c(
    "BRA_032_04_0198",
    "BRA_032_06_0669",
    "BRA_032_17_3288",
    "BRA_032_25_5212"
  ),
  Place = c(
    "Tefe, Amazonas",
    "Crateus, Ceara",
    "Petrolina, Pernambuco",
    "Sao Paulo, Sao Paulo"
  ),
  `Why this ADM2` = c(
    "Amazon / high-rainfall setting, useful for seeing whether a large wet-region deficit is picked up.",
    "Semi-arid Northeast, useful for long low-rainfall spells.",
    "Sao Francisco valley / Northeast interior, useful for seasonal deficits.",
    "Southeast urban setting, useful for the 2014-15 water-crisis period."
  )
)

selected_monthly <- merge(monthly, selected_places, by = "region_id")
selected_monthly[, Place := factor(Place, levels = selected_places$Place)]

# -----------------------------
# Table functions and plot scales
# -----------------------------

# Standard HTML table styling for small diagnostic tables
show_table <- function(x, escape = TRUE, caption = NULL) {
  knitr::kable(x, format = "html", align = "l", escape = escape, caption = caption) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
}

# Same styling, with repeated ADM2 rows grouped into readable blocks
show_grouped_table <- function(x, group_col = "Place", escape = TRUE, caption = NULL) {
  group_values <- as.character(x[[group_col]])
  row_groups <- rle(group_values)
  table_data <- as.data.frame(x)
  table_data[[group_col]] <- NULL

  knitr::kable(table_data, format = "html", align = "l", escape = escape, caption = caption) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    ) %>%
    pack_rows(index = setNames(row_groups$lengths, row_groups$values))
}

# Shared scales keep colors comparable across figures
pct_label <- percent_format(accuracy = 1)
share_palette <- c("#fff5f0", "#fcbba1", "#fb6a4a", "#cb181d", "#67000d")
rain_palette <- c("#f7fbff", "#c6dbef", "#6baed6", "#2171b5", "#08306b")
percentile_palette <- c("#67000d", "#cb181d", "#fb6a4a", "#f7f7f7", "#9ecae1", "#08519c")
percentile_values <- rescale(c(0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.50, 0.90, 1))
z_palette <- c("#7f0000", "#b30000", "#ef3b2c", "#fcae91", "#f7f7f7", "#bdd7e7", "#3182bd", "#08519c")
z_values <- rescale(c(-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 4), from = c(-4, 4))

# -----------------------------
# Historical events for maps
# -----------------------------

# Event months for the 6-month z-score maps
map_events <- data.table(
  Event = c(
    "2012 Northeast drought",
    "2014-15 Southeast water crisis",
    "2023-24 Amazon drought"
  ),
  date_month = as.IDate(c("2012-12-01", "2015-01-01", "2023-12-01")),
  Context = c(
    "Long drought in Northeast and semi-arid Brazil",
    "Water-supply crisis in Southeast Brazil, including Sao Paulo",
    "Severe Amazon drought that later widened across Brazil"
  )
)

# -----------------------------
# Baseline calculations
# -----------------------------

# Mid-rank percentile: share below plus half of ties
midrank_percentile <- function(value, baseline) {
  baseline <- baseline[!is.na(baseline)]
  if (is.na(value) || length(baseline) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  (sum(baseline < value) + 0.5 * sum(baseline == value)) / length(baseline)
}

# Prior-20-year comparison for one rainfall window
rolling20_percentile <- function(data, rain_col, keep_place = FALSE) {
  # Place names are needed only for selected-ADM2 figures
  keep_cols <- c("region_id", "date_month", "year", "month_number", "Period")
  if (keep_place) {
    keep_cols <- c(keep_cols, "Place")
  }

  out <- data[, keep_cols, with = FALSE]
  out[, rain_mm := data[[rain_col]]]

  # Same ADM2 and same ending calendar month
  setorder(out, region_id, month_number, year)

  # Initialize rolling-baseline outputs
  out[
    ,
    `:=`(
      Percentile = NA_real_,
      baseline_mean_mm = NA_real_,
      baseline_sd_mm = NA_real_,
      baseline_min_mm = NA_real_
    )
  ]

  out[
    ,
    c("Percentile", "baseline_mean_mm", "baseline_sd_mm", "baseline_min_mm") := {
      pct <- rep(NA_real_, .N)
      mean_mm <- rep(NA_real_, .N)
      sd_mm <- rep(NA_real_, .N)
      min_mm <- rep(NA_real_, .N)

      if (.N >= 21) {
        for (row_id in 21:.N) {
          # Previous 20 years only, current year excluded
          baseline <- rain_mm[(row_id - 20):(row_id - 1)]

          # Require 20 calendar years, not just 20 rows
          has_20_prior_years <- year[row_id] - year[row_id - 20] == 20

          # Require all 20 prior rainfall values
          if (!is.na(rain_mm[row_id]) && has_20_prior_years && all(!is.na(baseline))) {
            pct[row_id] <- midrank_percentile(rain_mm[row_id], baseline)
            mean_mm[row_id] <- mean(baseline)
            sd_mm[row_id] <- sd(baseline)
            min_mm[row_id] <- min(baseline)
          }
        }
      }

      list(pct, mean_mm, sd_mm, min_mm)
    },
    by = .(region_id, month_number)
  ]

  out[
    ,
    # Standardized relative to the prior-20-year mean and SD
    z := fifelse(
      !is.na(rain_mm) & !is.na(baseline_sd_mm) & baseline_sd_mm > 0,
      (rain_mm - baseline_mean_mm) / baseline_sd_mm,
      NA_real_
    )
  ]
  # Rainfall deficit relative to the prior-20-year mean, floored at zero
  out[, deficit_mm := fifelse(!is.na(rain_mm) & !is.na(baseline_mean_mm), pmax(0, baseline_mean_mm - rain_mm), NA_real_)]
  out[
    ,
    deficit_share := fifelse(
      !is.na(rain_mm) & !is.na(baseline_mean_mm) & baseline_mean_mm > 0,
      pmax(0, (baseline_mean_mm - rain_mm) / baseline_mean_mm),
      NA_real_
    )
  ]
  out[
    ,
    # Below the minimum of the 20 prior same-calendar-month values
    record_low := fifelse(
      !is.na(rain_mm) & !is.na(baseline_min_mm),
      rain_mm < baseline_min_mm,
      NA
    )
  ]

  out
}

# -----------------------------
# Episode definitions
# -----------------------------

# One-month drought episodes require at least two consecutive low-rainfall months
episode_table <- function(data, label) {
  # Episodes use 1-month rainfall, not accumulated windows
  episodes <- data[
    window == 1,
    .(
      Place, date_month, year,
      low = Percentile <= 0.10,
      percentile = Percentile,
      deficit_mm
    )
  ]
  setorder(episodes, Place, date_month)

  # Missing percentiles break a drought episode
  episodes[, low := fifelse(is.na(low), FALSE, low)]

  # Runs can continue across December-January
  episodes[, run_id := rleid(low), by = Place]

  out <- episodes[
    low == TRUE,
    .(
      start = min(date_month),
      end = max(date_month),
      months = .N,
      cross_year = min(year) != max(year),
      cumulative_deficit_mm = sum(deficit_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = .(Place, run_id)
  ][
    months >= 2
  ]

  # Some selected ADM2s may not have qualifying episodes
  if (nrow(out) == 0) {
    return(data.table(Note = "No episodes found with this definition."))
  }

  out[, Baseline := label]

  # Longest and largest-deficit episodes first
  out[
    order(-months, -cumulative_deficit_mm),
    .(
      Baseline,
      Place,
      Start = format(start, "%Y-%m"),
      End = format(end, "%Y-%m"),
      Months = months,
      `Crosses calendar year` = ifelse(cross_year, "Yes", "No"),
      `Cumulative deficit, mm` = comma(round(cumulative_deficit_mm, 1))
    )
  ][1:min(.N, 12)]
}

# -----------------------------
# Brazil map
# -----------------------------

# ADM2 shapefile uses the same region_id format as the drought files
prepare_brazil_shape <- function() {
  shape <- st_read(bra_shape_file, quiet = TRUE)
  shape$region_id <- sprintf(
    "BRA_%03d_%02d_%04d",
    as.integer(shape$ID_0),
    as.integer(shape$ID_1),
    as.integer(shape$ID_2)
  )
  st_crs(shape) <- 4326
  st_simplify(shape, dTolerance = 0.03, preserveTopology = TRUE)
}

# -----------------------------
# Fixed-baseline comparison
# -----------------------------

# Fixed baselines are only for this comparison
fixed_baseline_percentile <- function(data, start_year, end_year, label) {
  # Same ADM2 and ending month, but a fixed year range
  baseline <- data[
    year >= start_year & year <= end_year,
    .(baseline_values = list(rain_mm_06m_pop[!is.na(rain_mm_06m_pop)])),
    by = .(region_id, month_number)
  ]

  out <- merge(data, baseline, by = c("region_id", "month_number"), all.x = TRUE)
  out[
    ,
    `:=`(
      Percentile = mapply(midrank_percentile, rain_mm_06m_pop, baseline_values),
      Baseline = label
    )
  ]
  out[, baseline_values := NULL]
  out
}

# -----------------------------
# Diagnostic datasets
# -----------------------------

# Selected places, all rainfall windows
rolling_selected <- rbindlist(lapply(windows, function(window) {
  # Same prior-20 rule for each window
  rain_col <- sprintf("rain_mm_%02dm_pop", window)
  out <- rolling20_percentile(selected_monthly, rain_col, keep_place = TRUE)
  out[, Window := paste0(window, " month")]
  out[, window := window]
  out
}))

# First possible prior-20 comparison year
rolling_selected <- rolling_selected[year >= 1980]
rolling_selected[, Window := factor(Window, levels = paste0(c(12, 6, 3, 1), " month"))]

# Full Brazil 6-month measure for event maps
rolling_brazil_6m <- rolling20_percentile(monthly, "rain_mm_06m_pop")
rolling_brazil_6m <- rolling_brazil_6m[year >= 1980]
```

# 1. Overview

## Goal

The goal is to build rainfall-based drought measures at the ADM2-month level
and understand what each measure is capturing before choosing variables for the
annual mortality panel.

The core question is:

> Was rainfall unusually low for this same place, in this same season, and over
> this time window?

I use Brazil as the pilot to look at raw rainfall patterns and work through the
main choices: the rainfall window, the baseline, threshold choices,
monthly-to-annual summaries, and whether known drought episodes show up in
plausible places.

What we want to get out of this is a clearer sense of the baseline, the rainfall
window, and which annual summaries best preserve the monthly drought signal.

## Selected ADM2s

I use four ADM2s that cover different rainfall settings: Amazon, semi-arid
Northeast, the Sao Francisco valley, and Sao Paulo. The point is to look closely
at how the measures behave in places where rainfall levels and seasonality are
very different.

```{r selected-places}
# Four ADM2s used throughout the diagnostic plots
selected_places_table <- copy(selected_places)
setnames(
  selected_places_table,
  old = c("region_id", "Place", "Why this ADM2"),
  new = c("Region ID", "Place", "Why selected")
)

show_table(selected_places_table, caption = "Selected ADM2s")
```

# 2. Measure Construction

## Monthly Measures

Monthly rainfall in ADM2 \(i\), year \(y\), month \(m\) is:

\[
p_{i,y,m}.
\]

The moving rainfall total ending in that month is:

\[
A_{i,y,m,k}
=
\sum_{\ell = 0}^{k-1} p_{i,y,m-\ell},
\qquad
k \in \{1, 3, 6, 12\}.
\]

So:

- 1 month: current-month rainfall.
- 3 months: current month plus the previous 2 months.
- 6 months: current month plus the previous 5 months.
- 12 months: current month plus the previous 11 months.

The prior-20-year baseline changes over time. For each ADM2, calendar month,
and rainfall window, it uses the 20 years immediately before the current year.
The current year is not included.

Because Brazil starts in 1960, prior-20-year comparisons start in 1980. For
longer rainfall windows, the first few months of 1980 can still be missing
because the 1960 rolling totals need months before January 1960. Mortality data
start later (1997), so the regression period has the needed rainfall history.

For the prior-20-year baseline, define the comparison set as:

\[
B_{i,y,m,k}^{20}
=
\left\{ A_{i,s,m,k}: s = y-20,\ldots,y-1 \right\}.
\]

Let \(\mu_{i,y,m,k}^{20}\) and \(\sigma_{i,y,m,k}^{20}\) be the mean and standard
deviation of that prior-20-year comparison set.

The z-score and rainfall deficits are:

\[
z_{i,y,m,k}^{20}
=
\frac{A_{i,y,m,k} - \mu_{i,y,m,k}^{20}}{\sigma_{i,y,m,k}^{20}},
\]

\[
D^{mm,20}_{i,y,m,k}
=
\max\left(0, \mu_{i,y,m,k}^{20} - A_{i,y,m,k}\right),
\qquad
D^{share,20}_{i,y,m,k}
=
\max\left(0, \frac{\mu_{i,y,m,k}^{20} - A_{i,y,m,k}}{\mu_{i,y,m,k}^{20}}\right).
\]

## Rocha-Soares Comparison

The <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdeveco.2014.10.003" target="_blank">Rocha
and Soares (2015)</a> comparison is separate. It uses the same moving 12-month
rainfall total, but compares it with fixed 1981-2010 annual rainfall for that
ADM2:

\[
RS^{log}_{i,y,m}
=
\log(A_{i,y,m,12}) - \log(\bar{P}_i),
\qquad
RS^{pct}_{i,y,m}
=
100\left(\frac{A_{i,y,m,12}}{\bar{P}_i} - 1\right).
\]

Here \(\bar{P}_i\) and \(s_i\) are the 1981-2010 mean and standard deviation of
annual rainfall for that ADM2. The Rocha-Soares threshold is:

\[
RS^{drought}_{i,y,m}
=
1\left\{ A_{i,y,m,12} < \bar{P}_i - s_i \right\}.
\]

(this is not SPI)

```{r measure-table}
# Monthly variables considered for the annual panel
measure_table <- data.table(
  `Monthly measure` = c(
    "Rainfall total",
    "Percentile",
    "z-score",
    "Below 10th percentile",
    "Below 5th percentile",
    "Below prior-20 minimum",
    "Rainfall deficit, mm",
    "Rainfall deficit, share",
    "Rocha-Soares comparison"
  ),
  `What it tells us` = c(
    "Actual rainfall over the 1, 3, 6, or 12 month window.",
    "How unusual the rainfall total is relative to the prior 20 years for that ADM2, month, and window.",
    "How far rainfall is from the prior-20-year mean, in prior-20-year standard deviations.",
    "A lower-tail indicator for unusually low rainfall.",
    "A stricter lower-tail indicator. With 20 baseline years, this is a small tail.",
    "Rainfall below every comparable value in the previous 20 years.",
    "Millimetres below the local prior-20-year mean, floored at zero.",
    "The same rainfall deficit divided by the local prior-20-year mean.",
    "Separate rolling 12-month rainfall comparison using fixed-baseline annual rainfall."
  )
)

show_table(measure_table, caption = "Monthly drought measures")
```

# 3. Raw Monthly Rainfall

## Monthly Rainfall Heatmap

Raw monthly rainfall is our starting point. It has strong seasonality and a lot
of month-to-month variation, which is why the drought measures use moving
totals and local month-specific comparisons.

```{r raw-monthly-rainfall, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6.2}
# Heatmap uses raw 1-month rainfall before any baseline comparison
raw_rain <- selected_monthly[, .(Place, year, month_number, rain_mm_01m_pop)]
raw_rain[, Month := factor(month.abb[month_number], levels = rev(month.abb))]

# Tooltips keep the plot readable without labeling every tile
raw_rain[, tooltip := paste0(
  as.character(Place),
  "<br>Year: ", year,
  "<br>Month: ", Month,
  "<br>Rainfall: ", round(rain_mm_01m_pop, 1), " mm"
)]

# Tile view makes low-rainfall seasons and isolated wet months easy to spot
raw_rain_plot <- ggplot(
  raw_rain,
  aes(x = year, y = Month, fill = rain_mm_01m_pop, text = tooltip)
) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~ Place, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = rain_palette, labels = comma) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "mm",
    title = "Monthly rainfall in selected ADM2s",
    subtitle = "Actual population-weighted rainfall, before any drought threshold"
  )

ggplotly(raw_rain_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

## Monthly Rainfall Time Series

The same data are shown below as a time series. We expect it to be noisy: raw
monthly rainfall varies a lot within the year, which is why the drought measures
compare each month to the same calendar month in earlier years.

```{r raw-monthly-rainfall-line, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6.4}
# Same raw monthly rainfall, shown as a time series
monthly_line <- selected_monthly[, .(Place, date_month, year, rain_mm_01m_pop)]
monthly_line[, tooltip := paste0(
  as.character(Place),
  "<br>Month: ", format(date_month, "%Y-%m"),
  "<br>Rainfall: ", round(rain_mm_01m_pop, 1), " mm"
)]

# Line view makes long low-rainfall spells easier to see than the tile view
monthly_line_plot <- ggplot(
  monthly_line,
  aes(x = date_month, y = rain_mm_01m_pop, group = Place, text = tooltip)
) +
  geom_line(color = "#2b6c9e", linewidth = 0.28, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(color = "#2b6c9e", size = 0.35, alpha = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ Place, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Monthly rainfall, mm",
    title = "Monthly rainfall time series",
    subtitle = "Hover to read month-level rainfall values"
  )

ggplotly(monthly_line_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

## Annual-Scale Rainfall Time Series

This plot shows 12-month rainfall totals ending in December. Red points are
years where that December-ending 12-month total is below the prior-20-year 10th
percentile for that ADM2.

```{r december-12m-trend, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.6}
# December-ending 12-month totals approximate calendar-year rainfall
december_rain <- rolling_selected[
  window == 12 & month_number == 12 & !is.na(rain_mm),
  .(Place, year, rain_mm, Percentile)
]

# Mark years below the prior-20-year 10th percentile
december_rain[, low10 := Percentile <= 0.10]
december_rain[, tooltip := paste0(
  as.character(Place),
  "<br>Year: ", year,
  "<br>12m rainfall ending Dec.: ", round(rain_mm, 1), " mm",
  "<br>Prior-20 percentile: ", percent(Percentile, accuracy = 0.1)
)]

# Red points flag December-ending years below the local prior-20 cutoff
december_plot <- ggplot(
  december_rain,
  aes(x = year, y = rain_mm, group = Place, text = tooltip)
) +
  geom_line(color = "#2b6c9e", linewidth = 0.95, alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_point(color = "#2b6c9e", size = 1.1, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_point(
    data = december_rain[low10 == TRUE],
    color = "#b2182b",
    size = 1.75,
    alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Place, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "12-month rainfall ending in December, mm",
    title = "Annual-scale rainfall with prior-20-year low-rainfall years",
    subtitle = "Red points are below the prior-20-year 10th percentile"
  )

ggplotly(december_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

# 4. Rainfall Windows

## What The Rainfall Window Changes

This holds the place fixed and changes only the rainfall window. Each vertical
slice is the same calendar month in Petrolina, shown four ways: current month,
last 3 months, last 6 months, and last 12 months.

The 1-month measure jumps around because it only uses current-month rainfall.
The longer windows are smoother because previous months stay inside the total.
This is the mechanical persistence built into the drought measure.

Red means the rainfall total is low relative to the prior 20 years for the same
ADM2 and calendar month. Blue means high rainfall. White is centered at the
median.

```{r petrolina-window-tiles, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6.8}
focus_place <- "Petrolina, Pernambuco"

# Hold place fixed and compare all four rolling rainfall windows
petrolina_windows <- rolling_selected[Place == focus_place]
petrolina_windows[, tooltip := paste0(
  focus_place,
  "<br>Month: ", format(date_month, "%Y-%m"),
  "<br>Window: ", Window,
  "<br>Prior-20 percentile: ", percent(Percentile, accuracy = 0.1),
  "<br>Rainfall total: ", round(rain_mm, 1), " mm"
)]

# Same months, only the accumulation window changes
petrolina_plot <- ggplot(
  petrolina_windows,
  aes(x = date_month, y = Window, fill = Percentile, text = tooltip)
) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = percentile_palette,
    values = percentile_values,
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = pct_label
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Percentile",
    title = "Petrolina: same months, different rainfall windows",
    subtitle = "Prior-20-year baseline; longer windows smooth the signal"
  )

ggplotly(petrolina_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

## Six-Month Z-Score Heatmap

This is still monthly, it shows the continuous 6-month z-score for each selected
ADM2-month, before collapsing anything to annual variables. Dark red means the
6-month rainfall total is far below the prior-20-year mean for that ADM2 and
ending calendar month. Blue means rainfall is above that local baseline mean.
White is centered at zero.

```{r selected-6m-z-heatmap, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=7.0}
# Six-month z-scores show continuous severity, not only threshold crossing
z_heatmap <- rolling_selected[
  window == 6 & year >= 1980,
  .(Place, year, month_number, date_month, z, Percentile, rain_mm, baseline_mean_mm, deficit_mm)
]
z_heatmap[, Month := factor(month.abb[month_number], levels = rev(month.abb))]
z_heatmap[, tooltip := paste0(
  as.character(Place),
  "<br>Month: ", format(date_month, "%Y-%m"),
  "<br>6m z-score: ", round(z, 2),
  "<br>6m percentile: ", percent(Percentile, accuracy = 0.1),
  "<br>6m rainfall: ", round(rain_mm, 1), " mm",
  "<br>Prior-20 6m mean: ", round(baseline_mean_mm, 1), " mm",
  "<br>6m deficit: ", round(deficit_mm, 1), " mm"
)]

# Z-scores keep severity continuous instead of using only threshold cutoffs
z_heatmap_plot <- ggplot(
  z_heatmap,
  aes(x = year, y = Month, fill = z, text = tooltip)
) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~ Place, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = z_palette,
    values = z_values,
    limits = c(-4, 4),
    oob = squish
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "z-score",
    title = "Selected ADM2s: 6-month z-score by month and year",
    subtitle = "Continuous standardized rainfall deficit; no percentile filter"
  )

ggplotly(z_heatmap_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

## 1st Percentile

With a prior-20-year baseline, the 5th percentile is already a very extreme
cutoff. There are only 20 comparison years, so one prior value is 5% of the
comparison set.

For example, a July-ending 6-month rainfall total is compared with the 20
July-ending 6-month totals from the previous 20 years. A 5th-percentile rule
picks months where at most one of those 20 prior totals is lower.

That's why I don't use a separate 1st-percentile threshold here. With 20
comparison years, 1% is less than one observation, so not very interpretable as
a percentile. If we want something even more extreme than the 5th percentile, I
would define it directly as "below the prior-20 minimum" rather than call it the
1st percentile.

# 5. Baseline Choice

The prior-20-year baseline is the main comparison. The fixed baselines are shown
only to see how much the definition changes.

```{r baseline-choice-table}
# What each baseline is meant to answer
baseline_choice_table <- data.table(
  Baseline = c("Prior 20 years", "Fixed 1981-2010", "Fixed 1961-2010"),
  `Question answered` = c(
    "Was rainfall unusual relative to the recent local climate? The comparison period moves, so long-term drying can be partly absorbed.",
    "Was rainfall unusual relative to this ADM2's 1981-2010 climate? Later years are judged against the 1981-2010 climate.",
    "Was rainfall unusual relative to a longer fixed period? Less noisy."
  )
)

show_table(baseline_choice_table, caption = "Baseline options used in the Brazil pilot")
```

```{r baseline-comparison-data, include=FALSE}
# Use the same 6-month rainfall values under three baseline definitions
baseline_input <- selected_monthly[, .(region_id, Place, date_month, year, month_number, rain_mm_06m_pop)]

# Prior-20 values were already calculated in the setup chunk
rolling20_selected_6m <- rolling_selected[
  window == 6,
  .(region_id, Place, date_month, year, month_number, rain_mm_06m_pop = rain_mm, Percentile)
]
rolling20_selected_6m[, Baseline := "Prior 20 years"]

# Fixed baselines are diagnostic comparisons only
baseline_compare <- rbindlist(list(
  rolling20_selected_6m,
  fixed_baseline_percentile(baseline_input, 1981, 2010, "Fixed 1981-2010"),
  fixed_baseline_percentile(baseline_input, 1961, 2010, "Fixed 1961-2010")
), use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)

baseline_compare <- baseline_compare[year >= 1980]
baseline_compare[, Baseline := factor(
  Baseline,
  levels = c("Prior 20 years", "Fixed 1981-2010", "Fixed 1961-2010")
)]
```

## Selected ADM2 Baseline Comparison

`Usable months` is the number of 1980-2024 ADM2-months where the 6-month measure
can be calculated. The fixed baselines cover all 540 months. The prior-20-year
baseline has 535 because January-May 1980 do not yet have 20 complete prior
years for the 6-month window.

```{r baseline-summary-table}
# Count low-rainfall months within each baseline definition
baseline_summary <- baseline_compare[
  ,
  .(
    `Months below 10th pct.` = sum(Percentile <= 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Months below 5th pct.` = sum(Percentile <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Usable months` = sum(!is.na(Percentile))
  ),
  by = .(Place, Baseline)
]

# Shares use usable months so the prior-20 startup period is not counted
baseline_summary[, `:=`(
  `Below 10th pct. share` = percent(`Months below 10th pct.` / `Usable months`, accuracy = 0.1),
  `Below 5th pct. share` = percent(`Months below 5th pct.` / `Usable months`, accuracy = 0.1),
  `Usable months` = comma(`Usable months`)
)]
setorder(baseline_summary, Place, Baseline)

# Display names make the baseline comparison table easier to read
baseline_summary_display <- copy(baseline_summary)
setnames(
  baseline_summary_display,
  old = c(
    "Months below 10th pct.",
    "Months below 5th pct.",
    "Usable months",
    "Below 10th pct. share",
    "Below 5th pct. share"
  ),
  new = c(
    "6-month total<br>months below<br>10th pct.",
    "6-month total<br>months below<br>5th pct.",
    "Usable<br>months",
    "Share of usable months<br>below 10th pct.",
    "Share of usable months<br>below 5th pct."
  )
)

show_grouped_table(
  baseline_summary_display,
  escape = FALSE,
  caption = "Selected ADM2s: how the 6-month low-rainfall count changes by baseline"
)
```

```{r baseline-comparison-plot, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6.0}
# Annual count of low 6-month ending points, by baseline choice
baseline_year <- baseline_compare[
  ,
  .(`Months below 10th pct.` = sum(Percentile <= 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = .(Place, year, Baseline)
]
baseline_year[, tooltip := paste0(
  as.character(Place),
  "<br>Year: ", year,
  "<br>Baseline: ", Baseline,
  "<br>6-month ending months below 10th pct.: ", `Months below 10th pct.`
)]

# Compare baseline choices using the same annual count
baseline_plot <- ggplot(
  baseline_year,
  aes(x = year, y = `Months below 10th pct.`, color = Baseline, group = Baseline, text = tooltip)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85, alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_point(size = 1.0, alpha = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~ Place, ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 3), limits = c(0, 12)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Prior 20 years" = "#2166ac",
    "Fixed 1981-2010" = "#b2182b",
    "Fixed 1961-2010" = "#ef8a62"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "6-month ending months below 10th pct.",
    color = NULL,
    title = "How much does the baseline choice change the 6-month measure?",
    subtitle = "Selected ADM2s, population-weighted rainfall"
  )

ggplotly(baseline_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

The baseline choice changes the level of the 6-month low-rainfall count in some
years, but the main spikes tend to line up. That is reassuring: it means the
largest events are not just artifacts of one baseline choice. The baseline still
matters for years closer to the 10th-percentile cutoff.

# 6. Episodes From One-Month Rainfall

I construct episode measures only for the 1-month time window. The 1-month
measure tells us whether a specific month had unusually low rainfall, so I add a
consecutive-month rule to avoid calling one isolated month an episode.

For the 3-, 6-, and 12-month measures, persistence is already built into the
moving rainfall total. A 6-month value below the threshold already means the
previous 6 months were low as a bundle, so I do not add another episode rule
on top of it here.

In this table, an episode means at least two consecutive 1-month observations
below the 10th percentile.

```{r selected-episodes}
# One-month low-rainfall spells. At least two months required inside episode_table()
episodes_10 <- episode_table(rolling_selected, "Prior 20 years")

# Add line breaks only when the table has episode rows
if (!"Note" %in% names(episodes_10)) {
  setnames(
    episodes_10,
    old = c("Months", "Crosses calendar year", "Cumulative deficit, mm"),
    new = c(
      "Episode length<br>months",
      "Crosses<br>calendar year",
      "Cumulative 1-month<br>rainfall deficit<br>mm"
    )
  )
}

show_table(episodes_10, escape = FALSE, caption = "One-month rainfall episodes below the 10th percentile")
```

## Severe ADM2-Months

Threshold counts are useful, but they don't say how far below normal rainfall
was. This table shows the most negative 6-month z-score observations for each
selected ADM2.

```{r severity-measures-table}
# Pick the three most negative 6-month z-score months per selected ADM2
severity_examples <- rolling_selected[
  window == 6 & year >= 1980 & !is.na(z),
  .SD[order(z)][1:min(.N, 3)],
  by = Place
]
setorder(severity_examples, Place, z)

# Same ADM2-months under the Rocha-Soares comparison
severity_examples <- merge(
  severity_examples,
  selected_monthly[, .(Place, date_month, rs_drought_12m_pop, rs_pctdev_12m_pop)],
  by = c("Place", "date_month"),
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Put continuous severity, rainfall deficit, and RS status side by side
severity_table <- severity_examples[
  ,
  .(
    Place = as.character(Place),
    Year = year,
    Month = format(date_month, "%Y-%m"),
    `6-month total<br>percentile` = percent(Percentile, accuracy = 0.1),
    `6-month total<br>z-score` = round(z, 2),
    `6-month rainfall<br>mm` = comma(round(rain_mm, 1)),
    `Prior-20 mean<br>6-month rainfall<br>mm` = comma(round(baseline_mean_mm, 1)),
    `6-month rainfall<br>deficit<br>mm` = comma(round(deficit_mm, 1)),
    `6-month rainfall<br>deficit share` = percent(deficit_share, accuracy = 0.1),
    `6-month total<br>below all prior<br>20 values` = ifelse(record_low == TRUE, "Yes", "No"),
    `Rocha-Soares<br>threshold` = ifelse(rs_drought_12m_pop == 1, "Yes", "No"),
    `Rocha-Soares<br>pct. deviation` = percent(rs_pctdev_12m_pop / 100, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
]

show_grouped_table(
  severity_table,
  escape = FALSE,
  caption = "Selected severe ADM2-months"
)
```

## Agreement Across Time Windows

This table checks whether the longer windows are mostly repeating the 1-month
measure or adding a different signal. The first four columns show how often
each window falls below the 10th percentile. The last two columns show cases
where the accumulated rainfall window is unusually low even though the current
month alone is not below the threshold.

Those last columns are useful because they show why accumulated rainfall
measures matter. A current month can look normal while the previous 6 or 12
months are still unusually low.

```{r window-agreement-table}
# Put each rainfall window side by side for the same ADM2-month
agreement_data <- dcast(
  rolling_selected[, .(Place, date_month, year, Window, Percentile)],
  Place + date_month + year ~ Window,
  value.var = "Percentile"
)

# Keep months where all four windows are available
agreement_data <- agreement_data[complete.cases(agreement_data)]

# Longer windows can be below the threshold even when the current month is not
agreement_table <- agreement_data[
  ,
  .(
    `Share of months<br>1-month rainfall<br>below 10th pct.` = percent(mean(`1 month` <= 0.10), accuracy = 0.1),
    `Share of months<br>3-month total<br>below 10th pct.` = percent(mean(`3 month` <= 0.10), accuracy = 0.1),
    `Share of months<br>6-month total<br>below 10th pct.` = percent(mean(`6 month` <= 0.10), accuracy = 0.1),
    `Share of months<br>12-month total<br>below 10th pct.` = percent(mean(`12 month` <= 0.10), accuracy = 0.1),
    `6-month total below<br>10th pct., but<br>current month not below` = percent(mean(`6 month` <= 0.10 & `1 month` > 0.10), accuracy = 0.1),
    `12-month total below<br>10th pct., but<br>current month not below` = percent(mean(`12 month` <= 0.10 & `1 month` > 0.10), accuracy = 0.1)
  ),
  by = Place
]

show_table(agreement_table, escape = FALSE, caption = "Agreement across rainfall windows")
```

# 7. From Monthly To Annual

The main question for this pilot is how much of the monthly drought signal we
can preserve when we turn the ADM2-month measures into ADM2-year variables for
the mortality panel.

The table below lays out the annual summaries we are considering. Some are about
duration, some are about severity, and some are simple annual rainfall
comparisons.

```{r annual-measure-table}
# Annual variables considered for the mortality panel
annual_measure_table <- data.table(
  `Annual summary` = c(
    "Duration count",
    "z-score severity",
    "Worst z-score",
    "Worst percentile / below prior-20 minimum",
    "Rainfall deficit",
    "-log annual rainfall GS (QJE)",
    "Rocha-Soares threshold count",
    "Worst Rocha-Soares deviation"
  ),
  `What it means` = c(
    "How many monthly ending points crossed the low-rainfall threshold.",
    "For 1-month rainfall, adds up below-normal monthly z-scores in the year.",
    "The most negative standardized rainfall value reached that year.",
    "The lowest historical rank reached that year, plus whether rainfall fell below the prior-20 minimum.",
    "Missing rainfall in millimetres relative to the local baseline mean.",
    "A simple annual rainfall measure: lower annual rainfall gives a larger value.",
    "How many ending months were below the Rocha-Soares threshold?",
    "How far below normal was the worst rolling 12-month value?"
  )
)

show_table(annual_measure_table, caption = "Annual summaries we can build from monthly measures")
```

This follows the same broad logic as the drought-index papers: once monthly
low-rainfall periods are identified, the annual panel can keep both duration
and severity. Duration counts how long the low-rainfall signal lasted. Severity
uses z-scores and deficits to keep information on how far below normal rainfall
was.

I also include a simple annual rainfall measure from
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjag005" target="_blank">Gehring and
Schaudt (2026)</a>: annual rainfall in logs, multiplied by negative one. So not
a drought index, but a simple annual rainfall benchmark we can compare against
the other drought measures.

For z-score sums, I use the 1-month measure. That keeps the annual sum easy to
read: it adds monthly standardized deficits inside the calendar year. For the
3-, 6-, and 12-month windows, nearby ending months reuse much of the same
rainfall, so I keep the worst z-score instead of summing them.

The unfiltered 1-month version only looks at rainfall deficits. It adds up
every negative z-score in the year.

\[
\text{1m z severity}_{i,y}
=
\sum_{m \in y} \max(0, -z_{i,y,m,1})
\]

\[
\text{below-10 1m z severity}_{i,y}
=
\sum_{m \in y} 1\{pct_{i,y,m,1} \le 0.10\} \max(0, -z_{i,y,m,1})
\]

The second version focuses only on months that qualify as low rainfall.

```{r annual-summary-data, include=FALSE}
# Annual summaries use the ending month's calendar year
annual_window_summary <- rolling_selected[
  year >= 1980,
  {
    # Require all 12 monthly values before making annual summaries
    complete_year <- sum(!is.na(Percentile)) == 12
    if (complete_year) {
      list(
        # Number of monthly ending points below each threshold
        n_low10 = as.integer(sum(Percentile <= 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)),
        n_low5 = as.integer(sum(Percentile <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
        # Sum below-normal z-scores. Positive z-scores count as zero
        z_severity_all = sum(pmax(0, -z), na.rm = TRUE),
        # Same severity sum, restricted to below-10th-percentile months
        z_severity_low10 = sum(pmax(0, -z)[Percentile <= 0.10], na.rm = TRUE),
        # Worst point reached during the calendar year
        worst_z = min(z, na.rm = TRUE),
        worst_pct = min(Percentile, na.rm = TRUE),
        # Largest and cumulative rainfall deficits
        max_deficit_mm = max(deficit_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
        cum_deficit_all_mm = sum(deficit_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
        cum_deficit_low10_mm = sum(deficit_mm[Percentile <= 0.10], na.rm = TRUE),
        # Below the minimum value in the prior-20-year comparison set
        record_low_months = as.integer(sum(record_low == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE))
      )
    } else {
      list(
        n_low10 = NA_integer_,
        n_low5 = NA_integer_,
        z_severity_all = NA_real_,
        z_severity_low10 = NA_real_,
        worst_z = NA_real_,
        worst_pct = NA_real_,
        max_deficit_mm = NA_real_,
        cum_deficit_all_mm = NA_real_,
        cum_deficit_low10_mm = NA_real_,
        record_low_months = NA_integer_
      )
    }
  },
  by = .(Place, year, window)
]
annual_window_summary[, window_label := paste0(window, "m")]

# Show severe years without making the tables huge
top_annual_years <- annual_window_summary[
  window == 6 & !is.na(worst_z)
][
  order(Place, worst_z),
  .SD[1:min(.N, 4)],
  by = Place
][, .(Place, year)]
```

## Annual Candidate Measure Tables

The tables below focus on four years for each selected ADM2: the years with the
worst 6-month z-score. This keeps the table readable and lets us compare
candidate annual measures in years that look severe for each place.

Percentiles are still useful for defining thresholds. But with a prior-20-year
baseline, the worst percentile often becomes 0: it just means rainfall was below
all 20 comparable prior values. Once we are in that tail, z-scores and rainfall
deficits carry more information about severity.

In the first table, each value is a count out of 12 monthly rows in that year.
For 6- and 12-month measures, the month is the ending month of the rainfall
window.

```{r annual-candidate-table}
# Duration counts by window and drought threshold
annual_duration <- dcast(
  annual_window_summary,
  Place + year ~ window_label,
  value.var = c("n_low10", "n_low5")
)

# Human-readable column names for the duration table
setnames(
  annual_duration,
  old = c("n_low10_1m", "n_low10_3m", "n_low10_6m", "n_low10_12m",
          "n_low5_1m", "n_low5_3m", "n_low5_6m", "n_low5_12m"),
  new = c("1m low10", "3m low10", "6m low10", "12m low10",
          "1m low5", "3m low5", "6m low5", "12m low5")
)

# Keep only the selected severe years
annual_duration <- merge(top_annual_years, annual_duration, by = c("Place", "year"))
setorder(annual_duration, Place, year)
setnames(annual_duration, "year", "Year")

annual_duration_display <- copy(annual_duration)
setnames(
  annual_duration_display,
  old = c(
    "1m low10", "3m low10", "6m low10", "12m low10",
    "1m low5", "3m low5", "6m low5", "12m low5"
  ),
  new = c(
    "1-month rainfall<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.",
    "3-month total<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.",
    "6-month total<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.",
    "12-month total<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.",
    "1-month rainfall<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.",
    "3-month total<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.",
    "6-month total<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.",
    "12-month total<br>ending months below<br>5th pct."
  )
)

# Duration table compares how often each window crosses each cutoff
show_grouped_table(
  annual_duration_display[
    ,
    .(
      Place, Year,
      `1-month rainfall<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.`,
      `3-month total<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.`,
      `6-month total<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.`,
      `12-month total<br>ending months below<br>10th pct.`,
      `1-month rainfall<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.`,
      `3-month total<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.`,
      `6-month total<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.`,
      `12-month total<br>ending months below<br>5th pct.`
    )
  ],
  escape = FALSE,
  caption = "Annual duration candidate measures: number of monthly ending points below each threshold"
)
```

This table is mainly about duration. The 1-month columns count individual
low-rainfall months. The 3-, 6-, and 12-month columns count low accumulated
windows ending in that year.

One thing to notice: a year can look severe under the 6-month measure without
crossing the 12-month threshold. This is not necessarily a contradiction. A bad
half-year can be partly offset by wetter months elsewhere in the 12-month
window.

```{r annual-severity-table}
# Calendar-year rainfall benchmark from raw 1-month rainfall
annual_rain <- selected_monthly[
  year >= 1980,
  .(
    annual_rain_mm = if (sum(!is.na(rain_mm_01m_pop)) == 12) {
      sum(rain_mm_01m_pop, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ),
  by = .(Place, year)
]
annual_rain[, `-log(annual rainfall) (QJE)` := -log(annual_rain_mm)]

# One-month summaries preserve within-year monthly deficits
annual_1m <- annual_window_summary[
  window == 1,
  .(
    Place, year,
    `1m z severity` = z_severity_all,
    `1m low10 z severity` = z_severity_low10,
    `1m cumulative deficit, mm` = cum_deficit_all_mm,
    `1m low10 cumulative deficit, mm` = cum_deficit_low10_mm
  )
]

# Six-month summaries emphasize the worst accumulated spell in the year
annual_6m <- annual_window_summary[
  window == 6,
  .(
    Place, year,
    `Worst 6m z-score` = worst_z,
    `6m max deficit, mm` = max_deficit_mm,
    `6m below prior-20 min months` = record_low_months
  )
]

# Twelve-month deficit is an annual-scale accumulated rainfall shortfall
annual_12m <- annual_window_summary[window == 12, .(Place, year, `12m max deficit, mm` = max_deficit_mm)]

# Rocha-Soares variables are already monthly rolling-12-month measures
annual_rs <- selected_monthly[
  year >= 1980,
  .(
    `RS threshold months` = if (sum(!is.na(rs_drought_12m_pop)) == 12) {
      sum(rs_drought_12m_pop == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_integer_
    },
    `Worst RS pct deviation` = if (all(is.na(rs_pctdev_12m_pop))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      min(rs_pctdev_12m_pop, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  ),
  by = .(Place, year)
]

# Candidate annual measures for the same ADM2-years
annual_severity <- Reduce(
  function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("Place", "year"), all.x = TRUE),
  list(top_annual_years, annual_1m, annual_6m, annual_12m, annual_rain, annual_rs)
)
setorder(annual_severity, Place, year)

annual_severity[
  ,
  # Format only after numeric summaries are joined
  `:=`(
    `1m z severity` = round(`1m z severity`, 2),
    `1m low10 z severity` = round(`1m low10 z severity`, 2),
    `1m cumulative deficit, mm` = comma(round(`1m cumulative deficit, mm`, 1)),
    `1m low10 cumulative deficit, mm` = comma(round(`1m low10 cumulative deficit, mm`, 1)),
    `Worst 6m z-score` = round(`Worst 6m z-score`, 2),
    `6m max deficit, mm` = comma(round(`6m max deficit, mm`, 1)),
    `12m max deficit, mm` = comma(round(`12m max deficit, mm`, 1)),
    `-log(annual rainfall) (QJE)` = round(`-log(annual rainfall) (QJE)`, 3),
    `Worst RS pct deviation` = percent(`Worst RS pct deviation` / 100, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
]
setnames(annual_severity, "year", "Year")

# Reader-facing names for candidate annual drought measures
annual_severity_display <- copy(annual_severity)
setnames(
  annual_severity_display,
  old = c(
    "1m z severity",
    "1m low10 z severity",
    "1m cumulative deficit, mm",
    "1m low10 cumulative deficit, mm",
    "Worst 6m z-score",
    "6m max deficit, mm",
    "12m max deficit, mm",
    "6m below prior-20 min months",
    "-log(annual rainfall) (QJE)",
    "RS threshold months",
    "Worst RS pct deviation"
  ),
  new = c(
    "1-month rainfall<br>sum of below-normal<br>z-scores",
    "1-month rainfall<br>sum below-normal z-scores<br>below 10th pct.",
    "1-month rainfall<br>cumulative deficit<br>mm",
    "1-month rainfall<br>cumulative deficit<br>below 10th pct.<br>mm",
    "Worst 6-month<br>z-score",
    "Largest 6-month<br>rainfall deficit<br>mm",
    "Largest 12-month<br>rainfall deficit<br>mm",
    "6-month total<br>below prior-20 min<br>ending months",
    "-log annual rainfall<br>GS (QJE)",
    "Rocha-Soares<br>threshold months",
    "Worst Rocha-Soares<br>pct. deviation"
  )
)

# Keep the main annual candidates together for the selected severe years
show_grouped_table(
  annual_severity_display[
    ,
    .(
      Place, Year,
      `1-month rainfall<br>sum of below-normal<br>z-scores`,
      `1-month rainfall<br>sum below-normal z-scores<br>below 10th pct.`,
      `1-month rainfall<br>cumulative deficit<br>mm`,
      `1-month rainfall<br>cumulative deficit<br>below 10th pct.<br>mm`,
      `Worst 6-month<br>z-score`,
      `Largest 6-month<br>rainfall deficit<br>mm`,
      `Largest 12-month<br>rainfall deficit<br>mm`,
      `6-month total<br>below prior-20 min<br>ending months`,
      `-log annual rainfall<br>GS (QJE)`,
      `Rocha-Soares<br>threshold months`,
      `Worst Rocha-Soares<br>pct. deviation`
    )
  ],
  escape = FALSE,
  caption = "Annual severity and comparison candidate measures for the same selected ADM2-years"
)
```

This table compares the severity measures we could carry into the annual panel.
The 1-month columns summarize deficits within the calendar year. The 6- and
12-month columns keep the worst rolling-window values, instead of summing
overlapping rolling windows. The last two columns show how the same years look
under -log annual rainfall GS (QJE) and Rocha-Soares.

One thing to notice: the largest 6-month deficit can be bigger than the largest
12-month deficit. That can happen because each deficit is compared with its own
baseline for that window. A very bad 6-month spell can still sit inside a less
extreme 12-month total.

## Annual Baseline Comparison

This table takes one possible annual measure, the number of 6-month ending
months below the 10th percentile, and recalculates it under each baseline. It is
asking whether the annual exposure changes when we change the comparison period.

```{r annual-baseline-summary-table}
# Recalculate one annual duration measure under each baseline definition
baseline_annual_summary <- baseline_compare[
  ,
  .(`Months below 10th pct.` = sum(Percentile <= 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = .(Place, Baseline, year)
][
  ,
  .(
    # How much annual exposure the baseline creates
    `Mean months per year` = round(mean(`Months below 10th pct.`, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `Years with any 6m low-rainfall month` = percent(mean(`Months below 10th pct.` > 0, na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1),
    `Years with 3+ 6m low-rainfall months` = percent(mean(`Months below 10th pct.` >= 3, na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1),
    # Which year gets the largest count under each baseline
    `Highest-count year` = year[which.max(`Months below 10th pct.`)],
    `Max months in a year` = max(`Months below 10th pct.`, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  by = .(Place, Baseline)
]
setorder(baseline_annual_summary, Place, Baseline)

# Shorter labels for the table
baseline_annual_summary_display <- copy(baseline_annual_summary)
setnames(
  baseline_annual_summary_display,
  old = c(
    "Mean months per year",
    "Years with any 6m low-rainfall month",
    "Years with 3+ 6m low-rainfall months",
    "Highest-count year",
    "Max months in a year"
  ),
  new = c(
    "Mean 6-month ending<br>months below 10th pct.<br>per year",
    "Years with any<br>6-month ending month<br>below 10th pct.",
    "Years with 3+<br>6-month ending months<br>below 10th pct.",
    "Highest-count<br>year",
    "Max ending months<br>below 10th pct.<br>in a year"
  )
)

show_grouped_table(
  baseline_annual_summary_display,
  escape = FALSE,
  caption = "Selected ADM2s: annual 6-month low-rainfall summaries by baseline"
)
```

The main takeaway is that the baseline choice changes the amount of annual
exposure, but the biggest years often still line up. Tefe and Sao Paulo look
much less frequently below the 10th percentile under the fixed 1961-2010
baseline, while Petrolina is fairly stable. So baseline choice matters, even if
some of the main event years are the same.

# 8. Takeaways And Questions

## Where This Leaves Us

Hopefully, this gives a clearer picture of the various measures, and can help
decide which drought variables should move forward.

The remaining decisions are:

1. Baseline: are we settled on the prior-20-year baseline as the main version?
2. Thresholds: use 10th percentile only, or also keep 5th percentile as a severe cutoff?
3. Time window: emphasize 3-, 6-, or 12-month rolling rainfall for the main annual exposure?
4. Annual summaries: duration counts, worst z-score, largest rainfall deficit, 1-month cumulative deficit, episodes, annual rainfall benchmarks?
5. Simple annual measures: should Rocha-Soares and -log annual rainfall GS (QJE) be kept as comparison measures, or should they also be included as candidate regression variables?

# Appendix: Historical Events And Maps

## Historical Brazil Episodes

The point is to check whether the 6-month measure picks up known Brazil drought
episodes in plausible places.

Concretely, I use these events to ask: do known events show up as unusually low
rainfall? Do they show up in the regions where we expect them? Does the z-score
map help distinguish local severity from national extent? Are there cases where
the measure looks too broad, too narrow, or concentrated somewhere unexpected?

```{r historical-event-table}
# Events used as qualitative checks against known drought history
historical_events <- data.table(
  Event = c(
    "2005 Amazon drought",
    "2010 Amazon drought",
    "2012-17 Northeast drought",
    "2014-15 Southeast water crisis",
    "2023-24 Amazon drought"
  ),
  `Main region` = c(
    "Amazon basin, especially the southwest",
    "Amazon basin",
    "Northeast and semi-arid Brazil",
    "Southeast Brazil, including Sao Paulo and Cantareira",
    "North/Amazon, later widening across Brazil"
  ),
  `Check period` = c(
    "2005-07 to 2005-10",
    "2010-07 to 2010-10",
    "2012-01 to 2017-12",
    "2013-10 to 2015-04",
    "2023-07 to 2024-05"
  ),
  `Why included` = c(
    "Major Amazon drought with strong impacts on river levels, forests, fire risk, and transport in parts of the basin.",
    "Widespread Amazon drought, included so the Amazon comparison is not based only on 2005.",
    "Long multi-year drought in the Northeast and semi-arid interior, with persistent water-supply and agricultural stress.",
    "Southeast water crisis centered on Sao Paulo/Cantareira, with strong pressure on reservoirs and urban water supply.",
    "Recent severe Amazon drought, with very low river levels and broader low-rainfall conditions in 2023-24."
  )
)

show_table(historical_events, caption = "Historical Brazil drought episodes used as reference points")
```

## Event Maps

The maps show selected event months for the 6-month measure. The point is to see
whether unusually low rainfall shows up in the expected regions, and whether the
event looks regional or more widespread.

Color shows the continuous 6-month z-score relative to the prior-20-year
baseline. Dark red means unusually low rainfall and blue means unusually high
rainfall. Dark outlines mark ADM2s below the 10th percentile.

```{r brazil-spatial-check, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6.8}
if (file.exists(bra_shape_file)) {
  bra_shape <- prepare_brazil_shape()

  # Map scale is fixed across events for visual comparison
  z_pal <- colorNumeric(palette = z_palette, domain = c(-6, 3), na.color = "#d9d9d9")
  leaflet_map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas)

  map_groups <- character(0)

  for (row_id in seq_len(nrow(map_events))) {
    event <- map_events[row_id]
    group_name <- paste0(event$Event, ": ", format(event$date_month, "%Y-%m"))
    map_groups <- c(map_groups, group_name)

    # 6-month value ending in the event month
    map_data <- rolling_brazil_6m[
      date_month == event$date_month,
      .(region_id, Percentile, z, rain_mm, baseline_mean_mm, deficit_mm, record_low)
    ]

    map_shape <- merge(bra_shape, map_data, by = "region_id", all.x = TRUE)

    # Cap z-scores for the map scale only
    map_shape$z_map <- pmax(pmin(map_shape$z, 3), -6)

    # Dark outlines mark ADM2s below the 10th percentile
    map_shape$outline_color <- fifelse(
      !is.na(map_shape$Percentile) & map_shape$Percentile <= 0.10,
      "#4a0000",
      "#ffffff"
    )
    map_shape$outline_weight <- fifelse(
      !is.na(map_shape$Percentile) & map_shape$Percentile <= 0.10,
      0.9,
      0.15
    )

    # Popup keeps the main drought quantities together
    map_shape$popup_text <- paste0(
      "<b>", map_shape$NAME_2, "</b><br>",
      map_shape$NAME_1,
      "<br><b>Region:</b> ", map_shape$region_id,
      "<br><b>Event:</b> ", event$Event,
      "<br><b>6m percentile:</b> ", percent(map_shape$Percentile, accuracy = 0.1),
      "<br><b>6m z-score:</b> ", round(map_shape$z, 2),
      "<br><b>6m rainfall:</b> ", round(map_shape$rain_mm, 1), " mm",
      "<br><b>Prior-20 6m mean:</b> ", round(map_shape$baseline_mean_mm, 1), " mm",
      "<br><b>6m deficit:</b> ", round(map_shape$deficit_mm, 1), " mm",
      "<br><b>Below prior-20 minimum:</b> ",
      ifelse(
        is.na(map_shape$record_low),
        "Not available",
        ifelse(map_shape$record_low, "Yes", "No")
      )
    )

    # One layer per event month
    leaflet_map <- leaflet_map %>%
      addPolygons(
        data = map_shape,
        group = group_name,
        fillColor = ~z_pal(z_map),
        fillOpacity = 0.78,
        color = ~outline_color,
        weight = ~outline_weight,
        smoothFactor = 0.4,
        popup = ~popup_text
      )
  }

  # Show the first event by default and keep the others in the layer menu
  leaflet_map <- leaflet_map %>%
    addLegend(
      position = "bottomright",
      pal = z_pal,
      values = c(-6, 3),
      title = "6m z-score",
      opacity = 0.8
    ) %>%
    addLayersControl(
      baseGroups = map_groups,
      options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
    )

  if (length(map_groups) > 1) {
    leaflet_map <- hideGroup(leaflet_map, map_groups[-1])
  }

  leaflet_map
} else {
  tags$p("Brazil shapefile not found.")
}
```
